judged_text: Read-then-write without a transaction or unique constraint allows two concurrent requests adding the same guest to both pass the already-attendee filter and both insert

record.issue_text: Read-then-write without a transaction or unique constraint allows two concurrent requests adding the same guest to both pass the already-attendee filter and both insert

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the code first reads the booking and its current attendees, then computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering only against the *currently loaded* `booking.attendees`. It then performs a separate `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`. There is no transaction around the read+write and no server-side de-duplication of `guests` (the input schema is only `z.array(z.string().email())`, unlike the client-side refine), nor is `createMany({ skipDuplicates: true })` used. As a result, two concurrent requests can both pass the `!booking.attendees.some(...)` check before either write happens and then both attempt to insert the same attendee rows (leading to duplicates if no DB uniqueness, or a unique-constraint error if there is one). This matches the finding’s core issue: a non-atomic check-then-insert.
